answer: Each new agent mints a one-use admission cipher by hashing a recent unique work trace with a secret nonce, then posts it to a public registry and locks a deposit. To vote or withdraw, the agent must cross a settlement bridge that rejects any cipher already claimed by another address and delays release so peers can flag clones. The ocean of historical work traces stays searchable, so a farm that recycles the same traces fails the uniqueness check and forfeits the deposit.
